text:
jordan (Eng): Heads up- planning unpaid parental leave from 2028-01-15 to 2028-04-15. Two quick Qs: 1) Can I suspend my 401(k) contributions while on leave and restart exactly when I'm back? 2) I have an active 401(k) loan via Pinecrest. How do missed payroll loan payments get handled if there's no wage to withhold from? Any paperwork I should file now?

taylor-peopleops: Congrats! For (1) yes you can change your deferral to 0% before your LOA; just update Workday and hit the payroll cutoff. To restart on return you can submit another election or change in Workday any time. Note the payroll cutoff is two business days before run.

aaron-payroll: For loan repayments, if there's no payroll we can't withhold; that alone doesn't automatically trigger an offset. The plan's loan rules matter. Usually Pinecrest will allow short pauses if informed, but extended missed payments or separation may cause the plan to treat the outstanding balance as a distribution.

maria-hr: Employer match: match is only on compensable pay periods. So if your LOA is unpaid, the match pauses. Vesting continues per plan docs (no change to past vesting).

samira (Pinecrest Retirement): Hi all - Pinecrest here. Quick checklist:
- Provide LOA approval to benefits@redwood.com
- Include loan ID and last 4 SSN when you email loans@pinecrest.com
- We can set a documented suspension of payroll loan collections for LOAs under 6 months; beyond that we evaluate on case-by-case.
If loan goes unpaid and qualifies as a default per plan (typically after missed payments over a plan-defined period or termination), Pinecrest processes an offset and issues a 1099-R for the taxable deemed distribution. We also notify the employer before offset.

jordan (Eng): Is there any way to make up missed employee deferrals after I return? Like a one-time catch-up from a later paycheck?

aaron-payroll: You can't retroactively take deferrals from paychecks already paid out. You can increase your deferral percentage going forward, up to IRS annual limits. If you're near the limit, talk to benefits so we can run numbers.

taylor-peopleops: For minimizing default risk on the loan: submit LOA docs to benefits@redwood.com asap. We'll flag payroll and notify Pinecrest so they mark collections as suspended while you're on LOA. That documentation reduces the chance of an automatic offset.

benefits-bot: Reminder: 401(k) deferral changes must be entered by 17:00 PT two business days before payroll. LOA docs upload: https://intranet.redwood/hr/leave-upload

samira (Pinecrest Retirement): Suggested email template we like (paste into loans@pinecrest.com):

```
Subject: LOA - Jordan P - request loan suspension - 2028-01-15 to 2028-04-15
Body: attach company LOA approval PDF, include Loan ID: 84321 and last 4 SSN: 6789, expected return 2028-04-15
```

maria-hr: We'll also offer a 15-min call with Pinecrest if you want to walk through tax implications. LMK and we'll schedule.

jordan (Eng): Thanks everyone, submitting LOA now and will email loans@pinecrest.com after benefits confirms. Appreciate the help :raised_hands:
